_comment: Five scenarios, corrected in Stage 4 remediation pass 5 (Stage 2 amendment pass 4). FAILED APPROVAL IS NOT AUTOMATIC REJECTION: an approve call that cannot execute fails with a stable domain-conflict error and leaves the request REQUESTED, unchanged -- it never silently transitions to REJECTED. Only an explicit POST .../reject (a human, capability-holding decision) moves a request to REJECTED. This corrects the previous version of this file, which had voidApprove auto-downgrade to REJECTED on an execution-time eligibility-recheck failure -- state-machines.md SS2 said exactly that, and has itself been corrected (Stage 2 amendment pass 4) to match: a failed execution attempt is not an authorized decision that the request should never proceed.

scenario_A_no_current_open_shift_at_appr._comment: Tests the EXECUTING terminal's own current shift/fiscal_day (state-machines.md SS2's condition 6 -- transient/operational, unrelated to which specific fiscal day the original sale belongs to). Two outcomes for the SAME request, depending on what's true at the moment approve is called.

sub_case_1_no_shift_reopened_yet.description: By 18:10, terminal-1 has no OPEN shift at all. voidApprove's execution-time recheck of the executing terminal's own context fails. This is a 409, not a 200 -- the void is left completely unchanged, still REQUESTED. The manager can open a new shift and retry with the SAME Idempotency-Key.

error.message: The approving terminal has no open shift; open a shift before approving this void.

sub_case_1_no_shift_reopened_yet._note: void-20 is untouched: status is still REQUESTED, requested_by/requested_at unchanged, approved_by/resolved_at still null, no stock_movement, no audit_event, no electronic_journal_entry. Retrying this exact call (same Idempotency-Key) after opening a shift is the intended path -- no fiscal mutation was committed, so no idempotency_record permanently consumed the key.

sub_case_2_a_new_shift_opened_by_approva.description: By 18:10, terminal-1 has since opened shift-B (a new cashier's shift, same calendar day). This condition is satisfied now, so voidApprove proceeds -- using shift-B/its fiscal_day, the CURRENT context at execution, never shift-A. (Contrast with scenario B: this succeeds only because the ORIGINAL SALE's own fiscal_day is unaffected here -- shift-A and shift-B belong to the SAME still-open fiscal_day. If the fiscal_day itself had Z-closed and reopened as a new fiscal_day, see scenario B instead.)
sub_case_2_a_new_shift_opened_by_approva._note: shift_id is shift-B, not shift-A -- proving the request-time shift is never reserved or frozen for later approval; only the shift open AT THE MOMENT of this approve call is ever used.

scenario_B_voids_originating_fiscal_day_._comment: Tests the ORIGINAL SALE's own fiscal_day (state-machines.md SS1's REQUESTED guard / SS2's re-checked eligibility condition -- 'sale's fiscal_day.status=OPEN'). Unlike scenario A, this is PERMANENT, not transient: once the sale's own fiscal_day Z-closes, RMO 24-2023 treats that business day's adjustments as closed -- no later fiscal_day, however valid, can ever make this void executable again. The void stays REQUESTED indefinitely unless explicitly rejected.
timeline: Day 1, 19:50 -- POST /sales/sale-cash-24/void (terminal-1, fiscal_day fd-day1 open) -> void-24 REQUESTED
Day 1, 21:00 -- POST /fiscal-days/fd-day1/close -- Day 1's Z-Reading generated; fd-day1 now CLOSED (sale-cash-24's own originating fiscal_day)
Day 2, 09:20 -- terminal-1 opens shift-C, which opens Day 2's fiscal_day fd-day2 -- a perfectly valid, OPEN current context
Day 2, 09:25 -- POST /voids/void-24/approve attempted, from terminal-1, with fd-day2/shift-C open

error.message: The originating sale's fiscal day has since closed; this sale can no longer be voided.

scenario_B_voids_originating_fiscal_day_._note: fd-day2/shift-C being open does NOT help -- this failure is about sale-cash-24's OWN originating fiscal_day (fd-day1), a condition entirely independent of the executing terminal's current context (scenario A's concern). void-24 is never attributed to fd-day2 merely to make it executable; it is left REQUESTED, permanently unable to succeed via approve again (every future approve attempt against void-24 will fail identically, since fd-day1 can never reopen). The only way to resolve void-24 now is an explicit POST /voids/void-24/reject by an authorized actor. This is exactly why Void requires the *original* sale's fiscal_day to still be open (state-machines.md SS1/SS2) while Refund does not (SS3) -- see scenario C.

scenario_C_refund_against_old_sale_succe._comment: Refund has NO eligibility condition tying to the ORIGINAL sale's fiscal_day (state-machines.md SS3: 'Unlike Void, Refund has no eligibility condition requiring the original sale's fiscal day to still be open') -- only to the EXECUTING terminal's own fiscal_day right now. This is the Monday-sale/Friday-refund pattern, applied here to request-vs-approval instead of sale-vs-refund.
timeline: Mon 19:50 -- POST /sales/sale-cash-21/refunds -> refund-21 REQUESTED (Monday's fiscal_day fd-mon still open)
Mon 21:00 -- POST /fiscal-days/fd-mon/close -- Monday's Z-Reading generated; fd-mon now CLOSED
Tue 09:15 -- terminal-1 opens shift-C, which auto-opens Tuesday's fiscal_day fd-tue
scenario_C_refund_against_old_sale_succe._note: fiscal_day_id is fd-2026-09-16-terminal-1 (Tuesday's), never Monday's already-closed fd-mon. The refund PERMANENTLY REFERENCES the original sale/sale_items from Monday's fiscal_day (sale_id: sale-cash-21, unchanged) while its own PROCESSING CONTEXT is Tuesday's terminal/shift/fiscal_day -- both stay visible and distinct in this response, exactly why Void/Refund processing context is independent of the original sale's context (Stage 2 amendment pass 3). Contrast directly with scenario B: the same 'original day closed, later day open' shape succeeds here for Refund and permanently fails for Void, because Stage 2 deliberately gives them different eligibility rules, not because of any Stage 4 API inconsistency.

scenario_D_concurrent_refund_consumes_qu._comment: Two refund requests against the SAME sale_item are both pending simultaneously -- both pass request-time validation, because neither has produced refund_item rows yet (state-machines.md SS3: refund_item rows are only created at APPROVED -> COMPLETED). Whichever gets approved FIRST consumes the quantity; the second approval attempt must re-validate against what NOW exists, not what existed at ITS OWN request time.
scenario_D_concurrent_refund_consumes_qu.setup: sale_item si-cash-22-1: quantity 2.000, net_line_amount 200.00 (unit_refund_amount 100.00/unit). Two refunds requested independently: refund-22a (quantity 1.500) and refund-22b (quantity 1.000) -- 1.500 + 1.000 = 2.500 > 2.000 available, but neither request was rejected at REQUEST time because no refund_item existed yet for either check to see.

error.message: Requested refund quantity (1.000) exceeds what remains for sale_item si-cash-22-1 (0.500), because a concurrent refund was approved first.

step_2_refund_22b_approval_now_fails._note: refund-22b is left completely unchanged -- still REQUESTED, no refund_item/refund_settlement/stock_movement created, no processing-context fields populated. A human must now explicitly reject it, or approve it again later if the customer's return is instead reduced to fit 0.500 via a NEW, separate refund request (this exact refund-22b row keeps its original 1.000 request). This is exactly why remaining-quantity/amount is re-validated at approval time, not trusted from the original request-time check (invariants #27/#28).

scenario_E_refund_completes_before_void_._comment: Cashier requests a Void; before a manager approves it, a Refund against the SAME sale is separately approved and completed. Void's execution-time eligibility recheck (state-machines.md SS2's own motivating example for re-checking at execution time: '...because... a refund could be separately approved, in the window between a void being requested and being approved') catches this -- one of the same three original eligibility conditions as scenario B, just a different one of the three ('no COMPLETED refund exists against the sale' rather than 'sale's fiscal_day still OPEN'). Same corrected outcome as scenario B: a stable conflict, not an automatic rejection.
timeline: 10:00 -- POST /sales/sale-cash-23/void -> void-23 REQUESTED (sale-cash-23 still COMPLETED, no refund yet)
10:05 -- a separate Refund against sale-cash-23 is requested and immediately approved (requester held SALE_REFUND_APPROVE) -> sale-cash-23 now PARTIALLY_REFUNDED

error.message: A refund has already been completed against this sale; it can no longer be voided.

scenario_E_refund_completes_before_void_._note: void-23 is left completely unchanged -- still REQUESTED. sale.status is PARTIALLY_REFUNDED, proving the void never executed. Like scenario B, this is a PERMANENT failure for THIS void row (the completed refund never un-completes), resolvable only by an authorized actor explicitly calling POST /voids/void-23/reject -- never by the approve endpoint silently deciding the request is over.
